title: fix: open model setup directly when no models are available
body:
Fixes #200612

## What Problem This Solves

When the available model list is empty, opening the model control shows a large blank picker with a search field instead of taking the user to setup. This also happens on a clean installation with automatic account selection, even when no provider or account has been configured.

## User Impact

User impact: after the model list finishes loading and is confirmed empty, users can select **Set up a model** directly from the composer to open model-provider setup.

Loading, error, offline, restricted, locked, and pending-provider states retain their existing behavior. Personal/shared account recovery and other session targets keep the picker. No Gateway changes, configuration changes, or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing setup action and translated label rather than adding another setup flow. The shared model control chooses between the direct button and the picker in both existing chats and the new-session composer.

The earlier revision incorrectly treated the presence of any account section as a reason to retain the picker. The Gateway returns automatic account selection even before the first account is configured. The setup condition now accepts that selection while retaining the picker for a specifically selected personal or shared account.

The new-session page already shows its full-page setup action when no default model exists. The composer regression therefore also covers an empty available-model list with a configured default, where the shared picker is actually mounted.

## Evidence

Reproduced the reported automatic-account state before this repair: no models or configured default, no pending providers, and a successful catalog response opened the oversized empty picker. With the repair, the same existing-chat state opens **Add an account** directly. The new-session composer also opens setup directly by keyboard, and the existing full-page setup path remains working.

- All 246 focused unit/component tests across ten files passed.
- All 22 Chromium production-UI browser tests across the two PR suites passed with synthetic Gateway responses. The existing screenshots remain applicable because the bundle repair does not change the rendered controls.
- UI chat test typecheck, production UI typecheck, changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent read-only source review of the lazy shortcut, row registration, and focus relocation found no actionable correctness issues. Existing assertions remain intact.

Native macOS/WKWebView has not been rechecked on the repaired head. The supplementary Linux WebKit attempt timed out, so it is not passing evidence. The [hosted control-ui-performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44166170430/job/134333815071) passed on b0a2172fb6ef5a108fd48c411b0d761b9cd0bccf. This verifies the performance gate, not the status of every CI job. The separate permissions-popover issue is outside this change.

### Bundle-size repair

The [d30492d performance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44159700439/job/134310927958) fails on PR-added JavaScript. Daniel supplied the full-log comparison: largest ordinary JavaScript gzip is 572,366 bytes on base and 572,537 bytes on the candidate, against an unchanged 572,440-byte cap. Chat boot gzip is 1,325,469 -> 1,325,640 bytes, against a 1,325,580-byte cap. New-session boot is 815,913 -> 816,084 bytes. Both boot paths gain 171 bytes; request counts remain 21 and 17. Startup JavaScript and all CSS are unchanged. The CSS headroom warning also occurs on base; it does not explain these PR-added failures.

The repair moves panel-only shortcut registration, keyboard handling, row registration, search focus, and selection closing into the existing lazy panel owner. It removes duplicate eager DOM references and two callback props. The setup button stays synchronous. No new dynamic import, budget, CSS, or request-count change was introduced.

The normalized local comparison against pinned base 1d82bed0a7fef79012c38ea7e6184911aba27e63 passed with Node 24.22.1. Largest ordinary JavaScript is 572,103 bytes, 337 bytes below the unchanged cap and 288 bytes below the previous local 572,391-byte result. Chat boot is 1,324,940 -> 1,324,878 bytes (-62); New Session is 815,762 -> 815,639 bytes (-123). Startup JavaScript is 91,013 -> 91,020 bytes (+7), below its unchanged limit. Chat and New Session requests remain 21 and 17; all CSS is unchanged. The inherited CSS warning remains.

CI measurements are authoritative. The previous local and hosted byte counts differed; the numbers above remain explicitly local. The [hosted performance gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44166170430/job/134333815071) now also passes on exact published head b0a2172fb6ef5a108fd48c411b0d761b9cd0bccf, verified after completion with the PR still at that head. No latency claim is made.

<details>
<summary>Validation and simplification details</summary>

The automatic-account response matches the existing unconfigured Gateway regression. The browser fixtures now include a signed-in user so both composer entry points receive account-selection metadata. The personal-account recovery test retains its search and keyboard-selection assertions.

The final pr-simplify pass retains the direct setup condition and the earlier removal of redundant derived state. This follow-up moves interaction work to the panel that owns the input and rows, removing eager implementations, duplicate DOM references, and two callback props. The remaining eager delegates preserve the existing event and row-ref boundaries, including Solid's delegated keyboard event ordering. The six-file follow-up is production +137/-127 lines and tests +45/-3; the complete ten-file PR against the pinned base is production +202/-164 and tests +219/-25. Necessary growth is the direct setup action, its eligibility condition, and the typed lazy-view bridge.

Existing setup, recovery, loading, lock, provider, target, metadata, focus, and selection behavior stays protected. The added shortcut regression checks modified keys, IME composition, typing in search, nested menus, slash focus, and numeric activation. The existing production-UI browser flow now verifies shortcuts after a cold panel load, after reopening without another catalog request, and after filtering a large catalog. Earlier metadata regressions remain intact. Independent source review found no actionable issues; the author ran the tests and bundle measurements.

Local checks:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-model-catalog.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.test.tsx ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-catalog-state.test.tsx ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-picker.test.tsx ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-picker-search.test.ts ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control-view.test.tsx ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-model-runtime.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-provider-icon-lazy.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/chat-model-controls.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/chat-composer-catalog.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-chat.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.ui.json --incremental
```

The final focused run passed 246 tests across ten files, including the isolated provider-icon failure shard; the two PR browser suites passed all 22 tests in 40.94 seconds on this repair. Bundler workers were bounded and the existing browser-library/fontconfig setup was retained.

The full performance comparison used Vite 8.3.5, Rolldown 1.2.14, libdeflate 0.1.0 for normalized gzip, and the committed fixed build identity. The earlier 572,391-byte result was reproduced with both Node 24.20.0 and CI's Node 24.22.1; changing Node did not explain that CI difference. The final repair measured 572,103 bytes on Node 24.22.1. A proof-only copy of `scripts/check-control-ui-performance-base.mts` relocated its temporary baseline archive into the workspace because the sandbox temporary filesystem is limited to 1 GiB; import paths and the repository-root calculation were adjusted for that location. Workloads, compression, metrics, thresholds, and failure handling were unchanged. The current full comparison uses the exact published source tree and pinned base, but its local byte counts differ from CI as noted above. No proof adapter is committed.

Earlier CI follow-ups corrected the cold-catalog fixture without dropping assertions: it now sets `state.chatModelCatalogInitialized = false` after constructing the page fixture, rather than passing page-owned state through the narrower host override type. This addressed the [checks-ui failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44105567181/job/134117885674) and its subsequent TS2769 fixture error.

</details>

Co-authored with Dan.
